g: A prepackaged meal purchased chilled or frozen and heated at home.
(video games) An early type of video game, the predecessor of modern games consoles, consisting of a unit with a built-in controller that plugged into a television set.
(rare, usually non-native speakers' English) A home console game.
A book, magazine or website that lists the television schedule.
An interactive menu-based system displaying the television schedule on the television screen.
(colloquial) The world as depicted on television.
A movie made for and initially broadcast by a television channel.

(UK) The situation where a commercial break during a television programme adversely affects electricity generation and transmission as large numbers of people are operating appliances (kettles, refrigerators, etc.) at the same time.
A stand upon which a television is placed for viewing. The stand can be freestanding or designed to be attached to a wall.
A form of autistic echolalia involving the repetition of words or phrases from television.

(Canada, US, sports television) A time-out taking place during a televised sports match where the game clock is stopped for a period of time to allow for TV commercials to air before the resumption of play. A tray on which a meal can be informally served for eating while watching television.
(computing) A hardware component that allows a computer to receive television signals.
(computing, historical) A kind of video terminal that could be used with a standard television set.

(television) A female character archetype who is married to the main or co-lead male character, traditionally serving as either the grounded voice of reason in a sitcom or a complex partner in a drama.
(informal, rare) One who is addicted to watching television.
(mineralogy) A grey mineral containing mercury, antimony, arsenic, and sulfur.

(mineralogy) An orthorhombic mineral containing beryllium, calcium, hydrogen, manganese, oxygen, and silicon.
